newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian police uncover U.S. militia arms cache.
newsitem.headline: Canadian police uncover U.S. militia arms cache.

text.p: Canadian police said on Friday they had seized weapons and survival gear stockpiled by a right-wing U.S. militia group in a remote mountain area of northern British Columbia.

The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said they believed they had derailed efforts by the group to establish a camp near this small town close to the Alaska border, about 425 miles (640 km) north of Vancouver. They declined to identify the group or say where it was based in the United States.

"We have nailed this organisation at the grass roots in northwest British Columbia," RCMP Constable Len Meilleur told a news conference. "We feel we nipped this in the bud before anything could happen."

No arrests were made but Canadian and U.S. law enforcement agencies, including the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, were still investigating an unspecified number of suspects. All the suspects were in the United States.

In the raids, agents seized 15 weapons, mostly illegal, including assault rifles and a .50-calibre submachine gun, as well as hundreds of rounds of ammunition, including projectiles that burst into flames on impact, police said.

Police also found religious literature, sleeping bags, gas masks, chemical protection suits, detonation cables for explosives, dried food, stretchers and other first-aid gear. There were even toothbrushes and seeds to start gardens.
"These guys had everything," Meilleur said. "They needed nothing else to survive in the bush."

He said the group was not connected to a Washington state militia eight of whose members were arrested in Bellingham, just over the British Columbia border, by the FBI in July. Earlier media reports had speculated on a possible connection.
The Smithers cache was uncovered in police raids on a storage locker and trailer in July and August, but police did not release any information until they had investigated.
Local residents did not appear to be involved, police said. Smithers is a town of about 5,000 whose economy is based on logging, ranching and outdoors tourism.
In a statement, the police said it was the "first time they have disrupted a U.S. based outlaw militia group in Canada."

The news provoked alarm among British Columbians who fear an influx of U.S.-style violence. "It's quite frightening," RCMP spokesman Peter Montague said earlier. "We've never seen anything like this here."
